LESSON: FAITH AND GOD’S PROMISES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: THE BIBLE
Topic 2.1: Faith and God’s Promises

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Faith and God’s Promises. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you apply God’s promises in your daily life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the background to the call of Abraham
2. apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham
3. explain the importance of God’s promises to Christians today
4. apply God’s promises in their daily lives

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: FAITH AND GOD’S PROMISES
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Faith and God’s Promises helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: FAITH AND GOD’S PROMISES
Study Faith and God’s Promises like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the background to the call of Abraham

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the background to the call of Abraham. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the background to the call of Abraham.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Faith and God’s Promises” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the background to the call of Abraham. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham

What this means
In this part you learn to apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Faith and God’s Promises in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Explain the importance of God’s promises to Christians today

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the importance of God’s promises to Christians today. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the importance of God’s promises to Christians today.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the importance of God’s promises to Christians today. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply God’s promises in their daily lives

What this means
In this part you learn to apply God’s promises in their daily lives. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply God’s promises in their daily lives.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Faith and God’s Promises” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply God’s promises in their daily lives. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Faith and God’s Promises is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Faith and God’s Promises” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the background to the call of Abraham)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Faith and God’s Promises in your own words. (skill: apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: explain the importance of God’s promises to Christians today)

Example 4: Show how “Faith and God’s Promises” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply God’s promises in their daily lives)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Faith and God’s Promises to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the background to the call of Abraham.
3. Practise this skill: apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham.
4. Practise this skill: explain the importance of God’s promises to Christians today.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Faith and God’s Promises from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Faith and God’s Promises: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Faith and God’s Promises?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you apply God’s promises in your daily life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Faith and God’s Promises means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the background to the call of Abraham.
5. Be able to: apply faith in different situations as exemplified by Abraham.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
